description: An academically strong student who excels in theoretical computer science and high-level data structures but feels apprehensive about the transition to manual memory management and C syntax.

nodes.title: C Programming for Systems
nodes.description: Introduction to C pointers, memory allocation (malloc/free), and the toolchain required for systems development.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since this student has no prior exposure to systems programming, a primer on C is essential for completing the course projects.

nodes.title: Hardware/Software Interface Basics
nodes.description: Overview of how CPU, memory, and I/O devices interact, focusing on the hardware/software interface.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This student has no prior exposure to hardware concepts, making a high-level overview of computer architecture necessary before discussing kernels.

nodes.title: Understanding Kernel vs. User Mode
nodes.description: Visualization of privilege levels, the transition from user to kernel mode, and the role of the program counter during interrupts.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Visualizing mode transitions helps bridge the gap for a student with no prior exposure to operating system protection mechanisms.
Core content covering the essential services and system calls required for the first exam.
nodes.title: OS Services and System Calls
nodes.description: Exploration of standard OS services and the system call interface (API) used to request them.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Foundational core material on the process lifecycle that is required for all later scheduling topics.
nodes.description: Defining the process abstraction, the Process Control Block (PCB), and the state transition diagram.
nodes.title: Process Management and Lifecycle

nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard course requirement covering how independent processes coordinate and exchange data.
nodes.description: Methods for inter-process communication including shared memory and message passing via sockets.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)

nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement for understanding modern concurrent execution models and programming libraries.
nodes.description: Differences between kernel and user threads, threading libraries (Pthreads), and multi-threading models.
nodes.title: Threads and Threading Models

nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core topic involving analytical modeling of CPU efficiency and fairness.
nodes.description: Analysis of scheduling algorithms like FCFS, SJF, and Round Robin using performance criteria.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms

nodes.description: Comprehensive review of Chapters 1-5 material, including system structures, processes, threads, and scheduling.
nodes.title: Midterm Assessment Prep (Ch. 1-5)
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required midterm-review assessment checkpoint to ensure mastery of foundational material before the week 8 exam.
Core requirement covering the synchronization primitives used in programming projects and exams.
nodes.description: The critical section problem and the application of Mutex locks to prevent race conditions.
nodes.title: Critical Sections and Mutexes

nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard core material addressing complex synchronization challenges and classic theoretical problems.
nodes.title: Semaphores and Classic Problems
nodes.description: Advanced synchronization using semaphores and monitors, with a focus on the Dining Philosophers problem.

nodes.title: Deadlock Detection and Avoidance
nodes.description: Characterizing deadlock conditions and implementing avoidance algorithms like the Banker's Algorithm.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required floor block content for understanding system resource contention and deadlock prevention.
Core content essential for the memory management programming projects and final exam.
nodes.title: Paging and Physical Memory
nodes.description: Physical memory organization, address binding, paging, and page table structure.

nodes.personalizationRationale: Standard required material on how OSs manage limited physical memory via abstraction.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory & Page Replacement
nodes.description: Demand paging, virtual memory management, and page replacement policies like LRU and Optimal.
The I/O subsystem architecture, device drivers, and performance optimization techniques.
nodes.title: I/O Systems and Performance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required capstone block content covering the final stage of the OS architecture.
Standard core material on persistent storage management and file system hierarchy.
nodes.description: File system structures, implementation of directories, and allocation methods (contiguous, linked, indexed).
nodes.title: File System Implementation
Final Review (Cumulative)
nodes.description: Cumulative review of all course materials (Ch. 1-15) in preparation for the final exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required cumulative final-review assessment checkpoint to ensure comprehensive knowledge of the full syllabus.
